hero.name: Kelsey

narrative.title: Why Kelsey for Stryker Emergency Care?
narrative.highlight: Fire chiefs and medical directors want a rep who understands patient care, follows through on every order, and finds new business without being told where to look. I trained as an EMT in the ER and trauma bay, kept 100% of roughly 20 multi-million-dollar accounts at Goldman Sachs, and built a consulting practice from zero.
narrative.body:
My career started in client relationship management at Goldman Sachs, where I managed about 20 corporate lending accounts and kept every one of them with zero escalations. My interest in medicine led me to the UT Dallas EMT program. I finished in the top 5% of my cohort and trained alongside a medical director, physicians, nurses, and emergency medical services teams. My EMT and BLS training covered CPR, AED use, and chest compressions, the same areas Stryker's defibrillator and chest compression products serve.

I have not held a sales title. What I bring is the work underneath one. At Vivint I analyzed field selling performance and found a $2 million cost reduction and revenue opportunity that informed executive budget decisions. In 2023 I founded a consulting practice and grew it to 13 client families through referrals and outreach to parent groups. For 18 months I did volunteer outreach across a Spanish-speaking territory in Nebraska, Iowa, and South Dakota, met my assigned quotas, and generated more than half of my new commitments through referrals.

Stryker Emergency Care sells to people who make patient care decisions on municipal budgets. I want to be the rep who understands both the clinical side and the budget side.

startStories.ask: Achieve your assigned quota by taking a consultative approach to Pre-Hospital sales.
startStories.title: Quota attainment through a consultative approach
startStories.teaser: I met my assigned quotas across a three-state territory, with more than half of new commitments coming from referrals.
startStories.source: Spanish-Speaking Territory · Volunteer Service Representative · 2014 to 2015
startStories.experience:
For 18 months I did volunteer outreach across a Spanish-speaking territory in Nebraska, Iowa, and South Dakota. I worked against assigned performance quotas, planned each visit in advance, and reviewed it afterward to see what to change.

One community leader controlled access to local families and had shut out every representative before me. I did not push. I got to know his wife first, learned he missed playing soccer, and organized a pickup game. Over time he became my best source of referrals. More than 50% of my new commitments came through referrals, and I met weekly performance goals for 12 consecutive weeks while onboarding a new representative.
startStories.translation: A fire department that already runs another vendor's equipment is the same problem: a gatekeeper with no reason to change. I would learn what matters to the chief, the medical director, and the crews before pitching anything, plan every call, review it afterward, and let satisfied departments lead me to the next one.

startStories.ask: Become the resident Emergency Care expert as you work with fire chiefs, medical directors, clinical instructors and administrators.
startStories.title: Clinical credibility with a clinical audience
startStories.teaser: Top 5% of my UT Dallas EMT cohort, with training alongside a medical director, physicians, nurses, and EMS teams.
startStories.source: University of Texas at Dallas · EMT Program & Clinical Training · 2025
startStories.experience:
I finished the UT Dallas EMT program in the top 5% of my cohort and passed national NREMT testing. I trained with a medical director, physicians, nurses, and emergency medical services teams in clinical and trauma settings.

One night around 2am I was sent to the helipad with two nurses to receive an air ambulance patient. In the trauma bay the physician called for someone to cut the patient's clothes off. I stepped in while he performed an emergency tracheotomy, and the nurses told the other students to follow my lead.
startStories.translation: Fire/EMS buyers can tell quickly whether a rep understands patient care. I have completed the same EMT training many of their crews hold, I know the terminology, and I know what it means when a device adds a step during patient care. That lets me talk with a medical director about protocols and with a crew about workflow, and it gives me a base to become the expert on Stryker's products and on what competitors offer.

startStories.ask: Focus on customer satisfaction by solving problems through a consultative approach and providing a highly responsive and unsurpassed level of customer service.
startStories.title: Customer service that keeps every account
startStories.teaser: About 20 multi-million-dollar accounts at Goldman Sachs, 100% retained, zero escalations.
startStories.source: Goldman Sachs · Global Markets Analyst · 2021 to 2023
startStories.experience:
At Goldman Sachs I managed approximately 20 multi-million-dollar corporate lending accounts with a focus on customer satisfaction. I resolved client inquiries on loan terms, interest rates, and payment structures in partnership with support teams, and I never had an escalation across the portfolio.

If I gave a client a deadline, I met it, even when that meant working from a plane on Christmas Eve. When teammates were out, I covered their accounts too. I kept 100% of my book and received a performance-based bonus for customer service quality and operational accuracy.
startStories.translation: Fire and EMS agencies run around the clock, and a monitor or cot that is out of service is a problem that cannot wait. I would bring the same responsiveness: answer fast, bring in the right support team, close the loop, and keep the account for the next budget cycle.

startStories.ask: Address inquiries, negotiate pricing, and manage orders seamlessly. Take pride in cost reduction, and commit to on-time, complete, and error-free shipments.
startStories.title: Contracts, pricing terms, and error-free execution
startStories.teaser: I read 100 to 250+ page legal agreements so I would catch a problem before the client did.
startStories.source: Goldman Sachs · Global Markets Analyst · 2021 to 2023
startStories.experience: My accounts at Goldman Sachs ran on complex legal agreements of 100 to 250+ pages. I read every one front to back and translated the contractual terms, pricing, and payment structures into clear guidance for each client. My bonus recognized operational accuracy as well as service.
startStories.translation: Fire/EMS purchases move through municipal budgets, cooperative contracts, and grant paperwork. I am comfortable reading terms closely, understanding how pricing and payment structures work, and tracking an order until it arrives complete and correct.

startStories.ask: Display experience with reports and budget, customer service, and project management. Have basic knowledge of market research, new product introduction, and P&L management.
startStories.title: Reports, budget, and new product introduction
startStories.teaser: At Vivint I found a $2 million cost reduction and revenue opportunity and led the rollout of executive dashboards.
startStories.experience:
I started at Vivint without knowing SQL and was delivering executive reporting within nine days. Working in the data every day, I identified seven operational inefficiencies in field selling performance that added up to a $2 million cost reduction and revenue opportunity. The analysis informed executive budget and resource allocation.

I also developed executive dashboards and led their product introduction to the COO and six department leaders, who used them to monitor KPIs and sales targets.
startStories.translation: A department buys new equipment when someone shows the budget case: injury costs, maintenance, uptime, and what the purchase replaces. I can build that case with the customer's own numbers, track my own territory's numbers against target, and introduce a new product to a group of leaders in a way they will adopt. Running my own practice also gave me working knowledge of pricing and P&L.

startStories.ask: Promote and sell Stryker Emergency Care products to meet our customers' needs and drive business growth.
startStories.title: Business development from zero
startStories.teaser: I founded a consulting practice and grew it to 13 client families through referrals and parent group outreach.
startStories.source: Kelsey Tietjen Consulting · Independent Consultant · 2023 to present
startStories.experience:
In 2023 I founded a consulting practice specializing in private school admissions strategy and early childhood development for Dallas-area families. Nobody handed me clients. I went to parent groups to introduce the practice, and every engagement after that grew through referrals.

I secured 13 client families, managed engagements spanning 3 to 6 months, and earned repeat business from families who came back for another child. One student I worked with was admitted to a Dallas private school with a 15% acceptance rate.
startStories.translation: A territory is a book of business that someone has to build. I have already done that on my own, with my own name on the line. I would treat a Fire/EMS territory the same way: find the decision makers, earn the first department, and use that result to open the next.
